$schema_note: Phase 0 proof-of-concept dataset for the billionaire-government-money profile (docs/ideas/billionaire-subsidy-tracker.md). Subject is a named living person: every figure is source-linked. The unit of truth is the COMPANY and the AWARD; the person is a lens (founder + executive chairman + largest shareholder; stepped back as Amazon CEO in July 2021, remains exec chair; founder and owner of Blue Origin). Money TYPE values: FEDERAL_CONTRACT, FEDERAL_GRANT, FEDERAL_LOAN, TAX_CREDIT_SUBSIDY, STATE_LOCAL_SUBSIDY, REGULATORY_CREDIT. POLITICAL_SPENDING is money flowing OUT from Bezos / his companies, tracked here for the side-by-side, and is NOT government money received. NOTE: unlike the Musk profile, there is NO single published 'all-government money to Bezos' figure (no Washington Post-style aggregate). The headline below is the best-sourced subsidy aggregate (Good Jobs First, Amazon state/local subsidies) and is clearly scoped as such; it does NOT include AWS/Blue Origin federal contracts, which are listed separately as line items.
subject: Jeff Bezos

headline.label: at least $11.6 billion (Amazon state/local subsidies only)
headline.description: Cumulative state and local economic-development subsidies awarded to Amazon.com Inc. and its subsidiaries (warehouses, data centers, offices, film productions) per the Good Jobs First Subsidy Tracker. This is the best-sourced single aggregate available for a Bezos profile. IMPORTANT: it is NOT an all-government total — it EXCLUDES the large AWS and Blue Origin FEDERAL CONTRACTS (CIA C2S, NSA WildandStormy, JWCC, NASA Artemis, NSSL), which are services bought, not subsidies, and are listed separately below. There is no published Washington Post-style single 'all-government money to Bezos' number as there is for Musk.
headline.composition: ~20 state/local subsidy packages per year since 2012, dominated by warehouse distribution centers, with data centers (Amazon Web Services / Amazon Data Services) a fast-growing share; includes deals to subsidiaries (Whole Foods, Zappos, Audible).
headline.time_period: ~2000-2025 (Good Jobs First Subsidy Tracker, cumulative; figure as cited mid-2020s)
caveats: Good Jobs First calls subsidy totals a floor: many Amazon deals carry secret project names, NDAs, and undisclosed dollar amounts, so the true total is higher.

This is state/local SUBSIDIES (abatements, grants, tax credits) — categorically different from the federal CONTRACTS where the government BUYS cloud services (AWS) or a lunar lander (Blue Origin). Do not blend the two into one 'Bezos got $X' figure.
Subsidies are awarded/authorized multi-year values, not necessarily cash realized; some are abated taxes (money forgone), not checks written.
Subsidies flow to Amazon Inc. (a public company with millions of shareholders), not to Bezos personally; he is the founder, executive chairman, and largest single shareholder.
An earlier Good Jobs First / UNI Global figure was ~$4.7 billion globally (2020); the ~$11.6B reflects later cumulative tracking and the surge in data-center deals.

line_items.description: CIA Commercial Cloud Services (C2S) contract — AWS built a private cloud region serving the CIA and the broader U.S. intelligence community (incl. NSA). The deal that put a commercial cloud inside the IC; valued at up to $600M over its initial term.
line_items.value_basis: reported ceiling value of the C2S contract; IBM protested and lost the re-bid
line_items.notes: A federal CONTRACT (government buying cloud services), not a subsidy. Landmark deal: established AWS as the IC's cloud provider and anchored the later C2E multi-cloud procurement.

line_items.description: NSA 'WildandStormy' cloud-computing contract under the agency's Hybrid Compute Initiative. Awarded to AWS July 2021; Microsoft protested, GAO sustained the protest (Oct 2021), NSA re-evaluated and re-awarded to AWS in 2022.
line_items.value_basis: MAXIMUM POTENTIAL ceiling ('up to $10B'), not obligated dollars; classified scope
line_items.notes: Ceiling, not obligated. The exact value and task-order draws are classified; $10B is the widely reported ceiling. A federal CONTRACT, not a subsidy.

line_items.description: DoD Joint Warfighting Cloud Capability (JWCC) — a multiple-award procurement with a SHARED $9B ceiling across four providers (AWS, Microsoft, Google, Oracle). Replaced the cancelled single-award JEDI. AWS is one of four; its share is determined by individual task orders, not a fixed quarter.
line_items.value_basis: $9B is the COMBINED ceiling for all four vendors, NOT AWS alone; AWS's realized share is whatever task orders it wins
line_items.notes: Do NOT attribute the full $9B to AWS — it is a shared ceiling across four companies. A federal CONTRACT, not a subsidy. Successor to the cancelled $10B JEDI award.

line_items.description: NASA Sustaining Lunar Development (SLD) Human Landing System award — Blue Origin's Blue Moon lander selected as the SECOND HLS provider (alongside SpaceX), to fly a crewed demo on Artemis V. Firm-fixed-price; team includes Lockheed Martin, Boeing, Draper, Astrobotic, Honeybee Robotics.
line_items.value_basis: NASA-stated firm-fixed-price contract value; Blue Origin is also contributing significant private investment above this
line_items.notes: A federal CONTRACT (NASA buying a lunar lander), not a subsidy. NASA's own release states the $3.4B figure. Artemis 3/5 lander assignments were later subject to a 2025 program reshuffle.

line_items.description: U.S. Space Force National Security Space Launch (NSSL) Phase 3 Lane 2 — Blue Origin won the smallest share (~7 of ~54 missions) of a ~$13.7B three-way program (SpaceX up to ~$5.9B; ULA up to ~$5.4B). Blue Origin's first NSSL cohort entry (it was not in Phase 2).
line_items.value_basis: MAXIMUM POTENTIAL ceiling ('up to'), not obligated; individual mission orders follow as New Glenn certifies
line_items.notes: Ceiling value, contingent on New Glenn certification and task orders. A federal CONTRACT, not a subsidy.

line_items.description: Virginia incentive package to land HQ2 ('National Landing', Arlington): cash grants tied to jobs created plus state/local incentives, totaling as much as ~$750M. This deal PROCEEDED (unlike the cancelled NY half).
line_items.value_basis: ANNOUNCED/authorized value, largely performance-based (paid as jobs are created); realized value differs
line_items.notes: Performance-based: most of the Virginia package pays out only as Amazon hits hiring targets. This is a SUBSIDY (incentive to attract a facility), categorically different from the federal contracts above.

line_items.description: New York's incentive package for the other half of HQ2 (Long Island City, Queens): ~$1.5B+ in tax breaks, ~$325M in cash grants, plus other incentives — ~$3B total. Amazon CANCELLED the New York site in February 2019 after local political and community opposition.
line_items.agency: New York State + New York City
line_items.value_basis: ANNOUNCED package value — NEVER REALIZED; the project was cancelled, so $0 was actually paid
line_items.notes: CRITICAL: this $3B was CANCELLED and NEVER PAID. Listed for completeness (announced != realized). Must NOT be counted as government money Bezos/Amazon actually received. amount field is the announced package; realized value is $0.

line_items.description: Bezos's single largest known personal political donation: $10M to With Honor Action, a NONPARTISAN super PAC working to elect military veterans of both parties to Congress. (Bezos and then-wife MacKenzie gave a third of the group's ~$30M goal.)
line_items.notes: NOT government money received — this is Bezos spending. Notably NONPARTISAN (veterans of both parties), not a one-party play. This is his LARGEST-EVER direct political donation — orders of magnitude below Musk's 2024 giving.

line_items.description: Bezos and then-wife MacKenzie donated $2.5M to the campaign to uphold Washington State's same-sex marriage law (Referendum 74). An issue/ballot-measure donation, not a candidate or party donation.
line_items.notes: NOT government money received. A ballot-measure (issue) donation, not partisan candidate giving.

This is overwhelmingly Amazon's CORPORATE PAC, not Bezos's personal checkbook.

line_items.value_basis: company-confirmed donation; in-kind value of the Prime stream is estimated
line_items.notes: Corporate (Amazon) donation, not strictly Bezos personal, though widely read as a Bezos-Trump rapprochement gesture. NOT government money received.

caveats:
CRITICAL DISTINCTIONS (read before citing any number):

1. THERE IS NO SINGLE 'BEZOS GOT $X FROM GOVERNMENT' FIGURE. Unlike Musk (where the Washington Post built a ~$38B all-government aggregate), no comparable single published number exists for Bezos. The headline here is ONLY the Good Jobs First Amazon state/local SUBSIDY total (~$11.6B). It deliberately does NOT include AWS/Blue Origin federal contracts. Do not present the headline as 'all government money to Bezos.'

2. GROSS CONTRACT VALUE != SUBSIDY != PROFIT != PERSONAL INCOME. A federal CONTRACT (AWS's CIA/NSA/JWCC cloud deals; Blue Origin's NASA Artemis lander; NSSL launches) is the government BUYING a service or product at a negotiated price — most of it is spent delivering the work (engineers, data centers, rocket hardware). A SUBSIDY or tax break (HQ2 Virginia, data-center abatements) is closer to a gift or forgone tax — the government gets no direct service in return. Never collapse contracts and subsidies into one blended figure.

3. AWS CONTRACTS ARE SERVICES BOUGHT, NOT GIFTS. The CIA C2S, NSA WildandStormy, and JWCC awards are the government procuring cloud computing because AWS was judged the best/most-secure provider (each survived competitor protests). That is categorically different from a tax abatement handed over to attract a warehouse. Show the split.

4. CEILING / SHARED-CEILING != OBLIGATED != AWS-ALONE. The NSA $10B and the JWCC $9B are CEILINGS, not obligated dollars. Worse, JWCC's $9B is a SHARED ceiling across FOUR companies (AWS, Microsoft, Google, Oracle) — attributing the full $9B to AWS is wrong. NSSL Phase 3 Blue Origin 'up to $2.4B' is also a ceiling contingent on New Glenn certification.

5. HQ2-NEW YORK WAS CANCELLED. The ~$3B New York incentive package was announced in November 2018 and CANCELLED in February 2019 after local opposition. $0 was actually paid. It must NEVER be counted as money Bezos/Amazon received. Announced != realized — this is the cleanest example in the dataset.

6. SUBSIDIES ARE ANNOUNCED/AUTHORIZED, OFTEN PERFORMANCE-BASED. The Good Jobs First ~$11.6B is a floor (many Amazon deals carry NDAs, secret project names, and undisclosed amounts) AND a tally of awarded/authorized values, much of it performance-based (e.g., Virginia HQ2 pays out only as Amazon hires) or abated taxes (money forgone, not checks written). It is not cash-in-hand.

7. AGGREGATES CONTAIN THEIR LINE ITEMS — DO NOT DOUBLE-COUNT. The Good Jobs First ~$11.6B headline CONTAINS the HQ2-Virginia subsidy and the data-center subsidies listed below it. The 'amazon-bezos-2024-cycle' ~$17M contains family + corporate PAC giving. Summing the JSON 'amount' fields naively will over-count. Use the headline (for subsidies) and the individual contract line items (for federal contracts) separately; do not add everything together.

8. ATTRIBUTING COMPANY MONEY TO THE PERSON IS DEFENSIBLE BUT IMPERFECT — AND MORE SO FOR BEZOS THAN MUSK. Bezos founded Amazon, is its executive chairman and largest single shareholder, and founded and owns Blue Origin. BUT he STEPPED DOWN as Amazon CEO in July 2021 (Andy Jassy runs Amazon day-to-day), and Amazon is a public company whose subsidies also benefit pension funds, index investors, and millions of small shareholders. Blue Origin is privately owned by Bezos (cleaner attribution). The honest unit of truth is the company and the award; the person is a lens, with the control relationship stated, never an implied wire transfer to a personal account.

9. POLITICAL SPENDING IS MONEY OUT, NOT MONEY IN — AND BEZOS IS A NOTABLY LOW DIRECT DONOR. This is the key cross-partisan-balance point: Bezos's LARGEST-EVER personal political donation is $10M to a NONPARTISAN veterans super PAC (With Honor, 2018), plus $2.5M to a same-sex-marriage ballot measure (2012). That is orders of magnitude below Musk's $290M+ in the 2024 cycle alone. The 'nearly $17M' 2024 figure is Amazon's CORPORATE PAC plus family giving (mostly not Bezos personally), aggregated by an advocacy group. Amazon's $1M to Trump's 2025 inaugural is a corporate gesture. State plainly: as a DIRECT political donor, Bezos is modest and historically bipartisan/nonpartisan, NOT a mega-donor. Do not inflate this for symmetry with Musk.
